clue.text: Unsociable as a rugby-player?

indicators.note: as a means like a, which is what the suffix -ish adds to a word

parts.note: the stand-off is the rugby union fly-half, a back who directs play
the stand-off is the rugby union fly-half, a back who directs play

explanation.surface: A question about whether rugby players are a cold, unfriendly bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the stand-off is the fly-half; 'as a' gives -ISH, 'like', so the whole reads 'like a stand-off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof and reserved keeps others at a distance, which is what unsociable describes.

clue.text: Relax-there's a sort of strike

explanation.surface: Someone resting while a labour dispute goes on around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a seat is to rest or unwind; a protest where workers occupy the workplace seated is also called this.

clue.text: Put right, with me inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the word me is placed within another piece

parts.note: and can mean with, as in bread and butter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be included when a mistake is corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or rectify something is to change it for the better.

clue.text: Quarrel with party over the way

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it sits above, so comes first

parts.note: a disco is a dancing party
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out at a party about the route taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife or dissension between people is a falling-out or argument.

clue.text: Secure catch from shipping area

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed, secure
to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: Fishermen secure a haul from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: FASTNET is one of the sea areas named in the BBC Shipping Forecast, off south-west Ireland and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the named sea regions in the British Shipping Forecast, an example of the category.

clue.text: With determination, I get close to home

parts.note: taken as written
near means close by
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone resolutely heads for somewhere near home.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something seriously and resolutely means acting with sincerity and resolve.

clue.text: One is sure of a peaceful burial

definitions.text: One is sure of a peaceful burial

parts.words: One is sure of a peaceful burial
parts.note: plays on the idiom for making peace after a feud, in which an axe is buried, so this tool gets a peaceful burial

explanation.surface: A remark about someone guaranteed a quiet funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'bury the hatchet' is to end a quarrel, so the axe is the thing buried in peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A small axe is what the idiom about ending a quarrel says to bury.

clue.text: Part of horse is shrivelling

explanation.surface: A horse's body part is wasting away.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridge between a horse's shoulder blades has this name; a plant that dries up and droops likewise does this.

clue.text: City of London

parts.note: reads like the financial district known as the Square Mile, but means a separate city within greater London, home to Parliament

explanation.surface: A reference to London's famous financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City of London' suggests the Square Mile, but the clue means a city that lies in London: the City of Westminster, seat of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: It has city status and lies within greater London, so it is literally a city of the capital.

clue.text: Show symbol of authority, namely, before holding exercises

parts.note: SC stands for scilicet, Latin for namely

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other inside it

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
PT is physical training, exercises

explanation.surface: A ruler displays their regalia after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' reads as a link here, offering the definition that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch carries an ornamental staff as an emblem of sovereign power.

clue.text: Shift empty lorry in suitable way

parts.note: a shift is a stopgap measure, an expedient

indicators.note: an empty lorry has had its contents removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Advice to move an unladen truck efficiently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a verb or anagram signal, but it is a noun meaning a makeshift device.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting conveniently or advantageously for the purpose is acting in a fitting manner.

clue.text: Rate the first of September chilly

indicators.note: the first of picks out the opening letter of September

parts.note: chilly means cold

explanation.surface: A judgement that early September is cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' here is the old verb meaning to berate or tell off, not to assess.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone, in its old sense, is to reprimand them angrily.

clue.text: Now perish miserably in state of possession

indicators.note: miserably suggests the words are wretchedly mangled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dies wretchedly while possessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding title to property is the condition of having it as one's own.

clue.text: Race past island is friendly

indicators.note: past means the next piece comes after the island in the reading order

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea
kind means friendly

explanation.surface: A runner passes an island where the people are friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: The human race is the whole of humanity taken together.

clue.text: Little devil dying-hanging

parts.note: an imp is a small devil
dying, as of a day, is its ending

explanation.surface: A small demon expires on the gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to happen is said to hang over us, looming.

clue.text: Given attention-free of charge?

explanation.surface: A patient seen by the doctor wonders whether there was a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who has been given medical care, or a guest someone else paid for, has been handled this way.

clue.text: Block for student going to lectures?

definitions.text: Block for student going to lectures?

parts.words: Block for student going to lectures?
parts.note: block suggests an obstacle to attending, but means a pad of paper that a student takes to classes to write in

explanation.surface: Something that stops a student from attending classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper sheets is what a student jots on during lectures.

clue.text: Advertisement seen on back of car

explanation.surface: An ad stuck on the rear of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A film preview advertising it is one; a towed wagon hitched to the car's rear is another.

clue.text: Tug, hard at work pulling

indicators.note: at work means the letters are being worked on, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A tugboat working hard at hauling.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught horse is one used for hauling loads, so the word describes pulling.

clue.text: Greek character has list of data that may be changed

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a table sets out data in rows and columns

explanation.surface: A Greek has a spreadsheet that can be edited.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alterable or liable to change is described this way.

clue.text: President once crazy over only child

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above, so first

parts.note: mad means crazy
only suggests a single one, and one is I in Roman numerals
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A former head of state was mad about his only child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only child' looks like a single phrase, but 'only' gives I (one) and 'child' gives SON.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth US head of state, so he held that office in the past.

clue.text: Important leader is an egotist

parts.note: big means important
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A self-important boss described as vain.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited, self-important person is one with an inflated opinion of themselves.

clue.text: Bandit ran wildly from militia patrol

indicators.note: wildly suggests the letters run riot, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outlaw fled in panic from soldiers on patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: A trainband was a company of citizen soldiers in 16th-17th century England.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic English citizen soldiers were organised in such companies of trained men.

clue.text: Power? That's right, proverbially

explanation.surface: Someone checks a word and is told the proverb agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength or force is one sense; the saying that force makes right supplies the other.

clue.text: Good mark on examination

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A good grade on a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuous and ethical behaviour is righteous, upright.

clue.text: Going round with lots of money

explanation.surface: Someone driving around flush with cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel that turns over and over is revolving; someone 'rolling in it' is very wealthy.

clue.text: Sorry about church involved in witchcraft

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church apologises for its involvement in black magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic using evil spirits is the art of wizards and witches.

clue.text: Danger light activated at ninety degrees

indicators.note: activated suggests the letters are set in motion, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning lamp switched on at a sharp corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines meeting perpendicularly form a corner of exactly that size.
